title: Adapted cytokinesis-block micronucleus assay \(CBMn) for mouse embryonic stem cells
protocol: Prewarm all reagents for mESC culture medium preparation.
Aspirate all medium from the culture vessel.
Rinse the culture twice with 2 ml PBS-, gently rock the vessel for 30 sec and remove the buffer to dispose of all traces of medium containing FBS.
Add the appropriate amount of trypsin to each flask to cover the entire surface.
Incubate the culture at room temperature for approximately 1 minute.
Rock the flask back and forth 4-5 times quickly.
Wash the culture vigorously by pipetting the trypsin solution up and down over the cells.
Inactivate the trypsin by adding fresh, complete medium.
Triturate thoroughly to achieve a single cell suspension before inactivating.
Replate as desired.
Add 2 mM thymidine for 16 hours at 25-30% confluency of the stem cell culture.
Remove thymidine by washing with 1x PBS.
Add fresh KO-DMEM complete medium for 4 hours to release cells.
Treat ES cells grown on mEF with 4 µg/ml cyt-B for 14 hours.
Trpisinize the cells and spin them down at 800 g for 6 minutes.
Resuspend the cell pellet gently by tapping the tube.
Add about 4 ml of hypotonic solution.
Incubate the cells for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Spin down the cells again after incubation.
Fix the pellet with cool Carnoy's fixative (methanol: acetic acid; 3:1) for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Change the fixative twice.
Drop the suspension on wet slides previously cleaned with ethanol.
Air-dry the slides.
Stain the slides with Hoechst 33258 and rhodamin B.
Examine the slides under a microscope equipped with fluorescent optics (Olympus BX51).
Score cells blindly for MN presence.
Do not air-dry slides for longer than 10 minutes.
Store the slides in a microscope slide box in a cool, dry and dust-free cupboard.
Examine one thousand bi-nucleated cells per slide prepared per sample to measure MN formation.
Follow Fenech criteria for micronuclei screening.
Fluorescent stained slides can be stored at 4°C for up to 1 month.
Score MNi that are morphologically identical but smaller than the main nuclei, with diameters between 1/16 and 1/3 of the mean diameter of the main nuclei.
Distinguish MNi from artifacts by their non-refractile nature and lack of connection to the main nuclei.
Ensure MNi do not overlap the main nuclei, maintaining a distinguishable boundary.
Note that MNi typically have the same staining intensity as the main nuclei but may occasionally be more intense.
Use the t-test to evaluate MN formation induced by genotoxic agents.
